newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SOCCER-KAMAARK KEY TO SWEDISH SUCCESS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KAMAARK KEY TO SWEDISH SUCCESS.

text.p: Leicester City's Pontus Kamaark, who marked Brazilian star Juninho out of England's League Cup final this month, is counting on being as key an element in a confident Swedish side against Scotland on Wednesday.
Kamaark, back in the national team after a nightmare 18 months of injuries, has not played for Sweden since October 1995.

"It's great to be back and meet the guys again. It's almost like coming home," said Kamaark, hero of Leicester's 1-0 Cup victory against Middlesborough, when he marked the dazzling Juninho out of two games.
Kamaark's performance in England was so impressive that Svensson immediately called him up when regular backs Roland Nilsson and Teddy Lucic dropped out with injuries.
"I've worked like mad to get back in my club team and in the national team, but I have to say I didn't think I was going to get back in the national team this year," he said.
Kamaark said he was enjoying developing his attacking skills with Leicester but did not care where he played for Sweden.
"It doesn't matter where (trainer) Tommy Svensson puts me. I'll be working like mad to keep a regular place in the team." he said.

"We're really looking forward to this match, Now it's time for us to take revenge for all the knocks we took in the autumn," said Swedish trainer Tommy Svensson after a tough practice session in this western Swedish port on Sunday.
Sweden lost at home to Austria on October 9 and away to Scotland on Nov 10 and are third in the group.
Scotland lead it and a victory here would mean they would finish no worse than second in the group.
"We had a high intensity work out because the players needed a thorough shake-out," Svensson told reporters, adding his team would be at full strength for the match.
